preamble: Palatalization (secondary palatalization or 'softening') raises the body of the tongue toward the hard palate during the articulation of a consonant, typically before front vowels or a palatal glide. It is phonemic in Slavic languages such as Russian and Bulgarian and in the Goidelic broad–slender system of Irish, and automatic before front vowels in Lithuanian. It recurs across several Indo-European branches (Slavic, Baltic, Celtic) and is among the most widespread secondary articulations cross-linguistically.

examples.note: 'bee'; consonants are automatically palatalized before front vowels
